chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn Aynan, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) issued a ruling in the flood of Wadi Mahzur that for grain crops, the water is held back up to the shirak (a measure of depth/height), and for palm trees, up to the ka'b (a larger measure), then the water is released to flow below that.' Ibn Abi Umayr said: 'And al-Mahzur is the place of the valley.'

key_terms.اَلشِّرَاكِ: a traditional measure of water depth or height used in irrigation
key_terms.اَلْكَعْبِ: a larger traditional measure of water depth or height, greater than shirak
key_terms.وَادِي مَهْزُورٍ: Wadi Mahzur, a specific location mentioned in the narration

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on water distribution for irrigation according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith cites the Prophet’s ruling in Wadi Mahzur to establish precise irrigation limits—specifically distinguishing between grain and palm trees—thereby preventing upstream hoarding and ensuring equitable downstream access. This precedent underpins the Shia juristic principle of *haram al-huquq* (rights of others), emphasizing that water usage must not deprive others of their legitimate share, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic ethic of avoiding waste and ensuring communal justice.
